units.text: If you had a service-connected disability that limits your ability to work or prevents you from working, you may be eligible for VA Vocational Rehabilitation and Employment (VR&E) benefits and services, such as help exploring employment options and getting more training if needed.
units.reason: The context states that if you have a service-connected disability that limits your ability to work or prevents you from working, you may be eligible for VR&E benefits and services, including help exploring employment options and getting more training if needed.

units.text: Eligibility generally requires that you meet all of the following: you don't have a dishonorable discharge, you have a VA-rated service-connected disability of at least 10%, and you apply for VR&E services.

units.reason: The context lists these three requirements for veteran eligibility: no dishonorable discharge, VA-rated service-connected disability of at least 10%, and applying for VR&E services.

units.text: Your basic period of eligibility ends 12 years from either your separation date or your first VA service-connected disability rating, though this may be extended if a Vocational Rehabilitation Counselor determines you have a serious employment handicap.

units.text: If you're still on active duty, you may qualify if you have a 20% or higher pre-discharge disability rating and are about to leave the military, or if you're participating in the Integrated Disability Evaluation System (IDES) process or waiting for separation due to a medical condition from a serious injury incurred in the line of duty.
